tA.text: A · Folio — calm editorial, reading first

tB.text: B · Theatre — dark cinematic, the video as hero

tC.text: C · Signal — bold modern product, precise and vivid

sA.text:
Folio: the course as a well-set book.

Idea: lots of paper, one ink-blue accent, serif headlines that slow the eye down. The chrome stays quiet so the content (definitions, the lecturer's sentences, questions) is the design. The video is shown in a dark theatre; everything else is light.

Type: Newsreader (display; italic for emphasis), Inter (UI), IBM Plex Mono (sentence IDs, times).

Colour: paper #F8F7F4, ink #17191C, ink-blue #1F4FA3, marker yellow #FBE7A1 used only for what the learner saved.

Motion: slow and soft, 240-320 ms ease-out. Recap cards turn like pages (3D flip). Ask steps write in like a footnote list, then the answer sets line by line.

sB.text:
Theatre: a dark room where the lecture is projected.

Idea: the video is the hero and the rest is light thrown around it. Warm projector amber marks learning actions (continue, answer, save); a cool cyan marks the 'lab': maps and the model's process. Titles are set like film title cards.

Type: Instrument Serif (titles), Manrope (UI), JetBrains Mono (timecodes, IDs, the process trace).

Colour: room #0A0B0E, panels #14161B, text #EDEEF0, muted #9BA1AB, amber #FFB547, cyan #5CD3E6.

Motion: cinematic, 400-600 ms. Overlays fade up out of the paused frame; the recap is a deck you deal card by card; the Ask trace scans in line by line with a moving cursor.

sC.text:
Signal: precision and momentum (recommended).

Idea: a light, airy product with one vivid cobalt and a lime highlight for progress. Hairline borders, tight type, generous space. The player goes dark glass so the video still dominates. Reads as a modern tool, not a course site.

Type: Geist (everything; tight tracking at large sizes), Geist Mono (times, IDs).

Colour: ground #F5F6F8, white cards, ink #0E1116, muted #596171, cobalt #2E5BFF, lime #C8F169 (fills only, always with dark text).

Motion: quick and springy, 180-220 ms, staggered. Recap cards expand and their points reveal one by one; the Ask steps tick in along a progress rail; quiz options settle with a small spring.

mA.text: Motion (Folio, Activities): the timeline draws its hairline top to bottom as you scroll (300 ms per section). Opening an activity unfolds it in place, height-animated, 280 ms. Crossword: typing moves the cursor along the word; a finished word settles with a soft ink-blue underline that draws left to right; a wrong letter gets a 2 px shake, no red.

mB.text: Motion (Theatre, Activities): the timeline is a strip of frames; hovering a frame lifts it 4 px with an amber glow. Match the terms: drag a term onto a definition; a right pair snaps and both cards slide together and dim to amber outline (420 ms); a wrong drop springs back. The finished set plays a short shimmer across the strip.

mC.text: Motion (Signal, Activities): sections stagger in (40 ms apart). Crossword: the active word gets a cobalt band; each correct word fills lime from left to right in 180 ms; the clue list ticks the clue and moves it down. Completing the grid: the lime fills ripple once across all words.

kA.text: Ask (all three rows): click a sample question to play it. The steps are the real stream events of the saved answers in qa/answers.jsonl: one {event: step} per tool call (check_concept, lecture_dependencies) with its real result_summary, then {event: draft} streams the answer, then {event: done}. Citation chips are the answer's own (lecture N, m:ss) citations and open the player at that moment. Folio shows plain-language steps; Theatre also shows the raw tool call; Signal shows a progress rail.

nPh.text: Phone: the player is the whole screen; controls stay thumb-reachable at the bottom. Tap a caption sentence to save it (a toast shows the sentence ID and time). Activities rise as a bottom sheet over the paused video.
